key_insight: UPEBNL is a scalable causal Bayesian network framework that makes large EHR-based cancer prescreening more interpretable by learning stable dependency structures in parallel.
clinical_relevance: It could help clinicians and researchers understand which EHR factors drive risk predictions for esophageal and colorectal cancer, supporting more transparent prescreening workflows.
method: Adaptive data slicing to split large EHR datasets for parallel learning
Quality-aware structure aggregation to combine subnetwork results
Global DAG construction to produce a coherent causal-interpretable network
evidence_signal: In simulations, the method improved structural recovery by nearly 40% and was up to 221.28-fold faster; in EHR-based prescreening it achieved AUCs of 0.8171 for esophageal cancer and 0.784 for colorectal cancer.
watch_item: Because the causal directions are learned from observational EHR data, the resulting network may reflect associations rather than proven causation and still requires careful external validation.
paper_title: Scalable Causal-Interpretable Machine Learning for Cancer Prescreening Using Electronic Health Records
